newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Vefa to invest $600 mln, plans bank.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Vefa to invest $600 mln, plans bank.

text.p: Vefa Holding, a large Albanian business conglomerate, will invest $600 million in projects ranging from agriculture to tourism, newspapers quoted its president and owner as saying on Thursday.
"We shall invest $600 million this year," Koha Jone quoted Vefa president Vehbi Alimucaj as saying, adding that half of the sum had been obtained from foreign credits.
"It is to the benefit of the country that we are managing to attract money from abroad for our economy," he said.
Albanian authorities last year turned down a request by Vefa to open a bank, because they said staff were unqualified, but Alimucaj said Vefa would re-apply for the licence.
Speaking at an agro-industrial fair, he said more than $100 million would be invested in poultry, livestock and food industry projects.
Other projects would include construction of apartment blocks, a wood-processing mill, tourist complexes and infrastructure investment, he added.
